auth.title: OAuth guide | Ahrefs for Developers
auth.snippet:
All API calls require authorization and are made **on behalf of an authorized Ahrefs user**. To do this, your app must obtain an API **access token** for that user.
Ahrefs Connect uses **OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)**. The process has two main steps:
Redirect the user to:
```html
https://app.ahrefs.com/web/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id={client_id}&scope=apiv3-integration-apps&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}&code_challenge={code_challenge}&code_challenge_method=s256&state={state}
```
**Parameters:**
- `{client_id}` : URL-encoded Client ID from **Ahrefs Connect** section in your [Account settings](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/my-account).
- `{redirect_uri}` : URL-encoded Redirect URI you’ve registered in the same section.
- `{code_challenge}` : Derived from a **code verifier** using the S256 method:
- Generate a **code verifier** — a random string of 43–128 characters using a cryptographically secure generator. Allowed characters: `[A-Z] [a-z] [0-9] - . _ ~` (see [RFC7636 Section 4.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636#section-4.1)).
- Compute the **SHA-256** hash of the code verifier.
- Base64-URL-encode the hash.
- Use this encoded value as the `code_challenge` (see [RFC7636 Section 4.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636#section-4.2)).
- `{state}` : Generate an opaque value to maintain state between the request and callback. The authorization server will include this value when redirecting the user back to your app. (see [RFC6749 Section 4.1.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.1))
info
### Note for legacy app developers:
Both the legacy integration (API v2) and the new Ahrefs Connect (API v3) share the same OAuth client. This means they also share the same Redirect URI — you can’t configure separate production Redirect URIs for the old and new versions of your app.
We recommend updating the production Redirect URI in your Account Settings **only after** your new app has been reviewed and activated by Ahrefs, and you’re ready to release it.
If you prefer to keep using the same Redirect URI for both versions, you can use the `{state}` parameter to distinguish requests. For example, attach a unique string for the legacy app and another for the new app. Since the same `{state}` value is returned by the OAuth server when redirecting users back to your app, your server can branch logic based on this value. auth.title: How To Start - Ahrefs API
auth.snippet:
**Ahrefs API v2 has been deprecated**
This documentation is for the legacy version of our API (v2), which was discontinued on March 1st, 2024. Existing API v2 integration apps are not affected and continue to work as before, but new submissions are no longer accepted.

## Integrations - How to Start
API calls require authorization, and are made on behalf of an authorized user. In order to do that, an application will need to be granted an API access token from user. The procedure is different depending on the application type (web or desktop).
## For web applications:
- 1. Generate the "state" request parameter (opaque to the user) to maintain state between request and callback (see RFC6749 [section 4.1.1](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.1)).
- 2. Redirect the user to the invitation URL shown in [your apps list](https://cdn.app.ahrefs.com/api/integrations/apps-list), appending the generated "state" parameter to the request.
- 3. The user will see the authorization prompt. If he or she chooses to authorize your application to spend API rows, the service will redirect the user back to the redirect URL provided by you when [submitting your application](https://cdn.app.ahrefs.com/api/integrations/submit-apps).
- 4. Check the "state" parameter to make sure the callback was made for your request.
- 5. The callback request will include the "code" parameter your application must use when requesting the access token.
- 6. Send a POST request to [https://ahrefs.com/oauth2/token.php](https://ahrefs.com/oauth2/token.php) using the following parameters (see RFC6749 [ Section 4.1.3](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.3))
- grant_type=authorization_code
- code=<code from the previous step>
- client_id=<client id of your application>
- client_secret=<client secret of your application>
- redirect_uri=<redirect URI of your application>
- 7. If the access token request is valid and authorized, the service will return the successful JSON response:
```
{
"access_token":"<token you can use when performing API requests>",
"expires_in":<expiry interval>,
"token_type":"bearer",
"scope":"api",
"refresh_token":"<token you can use to retrieve the new API token>"
}
```
## For desktop applications:
- 1. Generate the "state" request parameter (opaque to the user) to maintain state between request and callback (see RFC6749 [section 4.1.1](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.1)).
- 2. Redirect the user to the invitation URL shown in [your apps list]

auth.title: docs.ahrefs.com/llms.txt
auth.snippet:
## Basics
- **Base URL:** `https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/{tool}/{endpoint}` (for example `https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/site-explorer/domain-rating`).
- **Authentication:** send your API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` header. Free "public" endpoints do not require a key. See [API keys creation and management](/api/docs/api-keys-creation-and-management.md).
- **Requests:** all data endpoints are `GET` with query-string parameters.
- **Responses:** JSON by default (`application/json`); most endpoints also support XML. Use the `output` parameter to choose the format.
- **Selecting fields:** most reports take a `select` parameter listing the columns to return; response cost depends on the rows and fields requested. See [Parameters](/api/docs/parameters.md).
- **Filtering:** rows can be filtered with a JSON filter expression via the `where` parameter. See [Filter syntax](/api/docs/filter-syntax.md).

auth.title: API keys creation and management | Ahrefs for Developers
auth.snippet:
You'll need an API key to send requests via Ahrefs API v3. Provide it in the Authorization header when making requests: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`.
## Creating API keys
Create and manage existing API keys in [Account settings / API keys](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys). Note that only workspace owners and admins have access to this section.
You can create up to 1,000 API keys. Each key has a lifetime of 1 year, after which it will expire and become inactive. You can see the expiration date for each key and who created it on this page.
A key will also be invalidated if the user who created it is removed from the workspace.

auth.title: Documentation - Ahrefs API
auth.snippet:
### Requesting Data
To retrieve data, an HTTP GET request must be sent to the API endpoint [https://apiv2.ahrefs.com](https://apiv2.ahrefs.com). Options (what kind of data to retrieve, the target and the mode of the operation, filters, sorting, etc.) should be passed as the request parameters. For example, to retrieve a maximum of 100 backlinks that links to ahrefs.com in XML format using the authentication token 012345, perform the following request to get data from the ***Backlinks*** table: [https://apiv2.ahrefs.com?from=backlinks&limit=100&target=ahrefs.com&mode=prefix&output=xml&token=012345](https://apiv2.ahrefs.com?from=backlinks&limit=100&target=ahrefs.com&mode=prefix&output=xml&token=012345)

protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#a9dadcd9d9c6dbdde9c8c1dbcccfda87cac6c496fadccbc3cccadd94e8f9e08c9b99fbccd8dcccdadd). We are more than happy to help you.
## Request Parameters
A request can have the parameters listed in the table below.
| Parameter | Mandatory | Default | Explanation |
|---|---|---|---|
| token | + | n/a | Authentication token |
| select | − | * | List of columns to select |
| from | + | n/a | Table to select data from |
| target | + | n/a | Aim of a request: a domain, a directory or a URL |
| mode | + | n/a | Mode of operation: exact, domain, subdomains or prefix |
| where | − | − | "Where" condition to satisfy |
| having | − | − | "Having" condition to satisfy |
| order_by | − | − | List of columns to sort on |
| limit | − | 1000 | Number of results to return |
| output | − | json | Output format: xml, json or php |
**!**Parameters must be encoded using UTF-8.
### • token
A token is used to authenticate and bill the user. Read more about the authentication process and how to obtain the token [here](/api).

access.title: Ahrefs SEO API: SEO & AEO Data API for Developers
access.snippet:
One SEO API to power all apps, agents, and workflows
Get access to Ahrefs’ world-class SEO & AEO API. Power reporting, dashboards, and workflows four ways: API, MCP, App, and Ask Ahrefs.

## SEO API Pricing
API access runs on usage-based units, not a flat per-endpoint fee, so light lookups and high-volume pulls both pay a fair price.
API access is included in every Ahrefs plan from Lite up. See limits:
| | #### Lite $129/mo | #### Standard $249/mo | #### Advanced $449/mo | #### Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rows per request | 100 | 250 | 500 | Unlimited |
| API units/mo | 200,000 | 800,000 | 2M | 4M, Custom |
| Custom API endpoints | | | | |
Not available on Ahrefs Free. Starter ($29/mo) includes [free test queries](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/free-test-queries) only.
Not sure how many units you need? [See how units are counted](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/limits-consumption).
The prices shown are exclusive of tax. Consumption tax will be added separately.

- Is there a free tier or test queries?
Yes, on any paid plan, as described above. Full production access at scale requires an [eligible plan](https://ahrefs.com/pricing).

access.title: Introduction | Ahrefs for Developers
access.snippet:
Ahrefs API is available on [eligible paid plans](https://ahrefs.com/pricing). On all other plans, you'll still have access to a [limited set of free test queries](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/free-test-queries).
## Plan limits
All requests besides [free test queries](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/free-test-queries) and the *Rank Tracker*, *Management*, *Public* and *some other* endpoints consume **API units**. The cost depends on the number of rows in a response and the fields requested. The minimum cost for any request is **50 units**. If an endpoint is free, you'll see a note about that on its documentation page; otherwise, it consumes units.

Please be advised that API units once consumed are non-refundable. We strongly encourage the use of our [complimentary test queries](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/free-test-queries) for all development and testing purposes to mitigate any unintended usage of API units.

[Eligible paid plans](https://ahrefs.com/pricing) include a monthly API unit allowance. On plans that support pay-as-you-go usage, additional units are automatically charged once the included limit is exceeded.
See also: [Pricing page](https://ahrefs.com/pricing) and [Account settings / Limits & usage](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/limits-and-usage/web).

access.title: Is it possible with a usual Ahrefs subscription to use your API functions?
access.snippet:
With a usual [Ahrefs subscription](https://ahrefs.com/pricing-plans) you will only be able to use OpenApp.
Each monthly package (***Lite***, ***Standard***, ***Advanced***,*** Agency***) contains certain amount of *OpenApp API rows*.
There are two cases when you can use OpenApp:
*1)* as a user, you can use one of the [OpenApp applications](https://ahrefs.com/apps) developed by our partners.
By using any of these application, OpenApp API rows included into your monthly subscription are consumed.
*2)* as a developer, you can [build your application using our API](https://ahrefs.com/api/openapp/how-to-start) and then submit and sell your app to thousands of our users.
If you need API data for your own internal needs or in-house application and want to make requests to Ahrefs API directly, you will need a separate [API subscription](https://ahrefs.com/api/subscription).
The smallest API subscription comes with 500K API rows included and costs $500/month.

mcp.title: What is Ahrefs MCP | Ahrefs for Developers
mcp.snippet:
**Ahrefs MCP** lets AI agents securely access the Ahrefs API and enrich their answers with real Ahrefs data. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard that allows AI tools to connect with third-party APIs in a secure, consistent way. In our case, it connects AI tools with Ahrefs, enabling things like this:
![](/images/db704fd04a1f2149.jpg)
## Connect to Ahrefs MCP
Ahrefs provides a hosted MCP server that allows users with a Lite plan or higher to connect their Ahrefs account to supported AI tools. Once connected, your setup is synced and available across all devices linked to your personal or company account.
### Connection URLs
- **Streamable HTTP** (recommended): `https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp`
- **Legacy SSE** (deprecated in many tools): `https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcpSse`
Most popular AI tools support connecting to the remote MCP directly. If you run into issues, check out our step-by-step setup guides:

- [ChatGPT Web](/en/mcp/docs/chatgpt-web)
- [Lovable](/en/mcp/docs/lovable)
- [n8n](/en/mcp/docs/n8n)
- [Manus](/en/mcp/docs/manus)
- [Mistral's Le Chat](/en/mcp/docs/mistral-le-chat)
- [OpenClaw](/en/mcp/docs/manus)
## API limits and usage
The remote MCP server is available on **paid plans starting from Lite.**
- Each plan has a **maximum number of rows per request** that an AI agent can access.
- Each plan also comes with a **limited amount of monthly API units.** The higher your plan tier, the more units are included. Enterprise customers can purchase additional unit add-ons if needed.
- When a third-party app makes an API call on your behalf, it consumes **API units** from your monthly allowance — the [same way as direct API usage](https://docs.ahrefs.com/docs/api/reference/limits-consumption).
You can track your current usage in **Account settings → [Limits and usage](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/limits-and-usage/web).**

When you connect Ahrefs MCP to an AI agent:
- You’ll see an **authorization consent screen.**
- Once approved, the connection will appear in your account with a dedicated **API key** (tagged with `MCP` scope).
- Workspace admins can set a monthly API unit limit for each key in the [API keys report](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys) to prevent over-usage.
You can also:
- **Manually generate an MCP key** in your account and use it in your AI agent’s configuration.
- Enterprise customers may also connect with their **API keys.**

mcp.title: Getting started with Ahrefs MCP
mcp.snippet:
The Ahrefs MCP server allows you to connect Ahrefs’ API to your AI tool of choice (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.)
No code required. Just chat in plain English to pull SEO insights, analyze competitors, create dashboards, and more — all within your AI chat interface.
## **What is MCP?**
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI models to connect with third-party APIs in a secure, consistent way.
## **What can Ahrefs MCP help me do?**
By connecting Ahrefs MCP to your AI tool of choice, you can:
- Pull Ahrefs data directly into AI-generated answers
- Automate exports without touching the API or having technical knowledge
- Combine multiple data sources into one request (without writing a programming script)
- Connect with other MCP-compatible apps
## **Which plans allow usage of Ahrefs MCP?**
Ahrefs MCP is available to users on Lite and higher plans. Below is a table listing limits across the plans:
| **Plan / Limits** | **API units** | **Max rows per request** |
|---|---|---|
| Lite | 200,000 | 100 |
| Standard | 800,000 | 250 |
| Advanced | 2,000,000 | 500 |
| Enterprise | Custom | Unlimited |
### About monthly API unit limits and Max rows per request
Each time AI tools call Ahrefs API via the MCP, it consumes API units. **One API call costs a minimum of 50 units**, with the exact amount depending on the complexity of the request.
​

You can use Ahrefs MCP with any AI tool that supports the Model Context Protocol. Popular options include:
- ChatGPT
- Copilot
- Lovable
- n8n
- Opencrawl
Note that each AI platform may have their own plan limits of what is required. [View the documentation](https://docs.ahrefs.com/docs/mcp/reference/introduction) for more detailed setup guides of setting up MCP for specific platforms.

### Can I run Ahrefs MCP in a local setup?
Local MCP setup is no longer supported. We only support remote MCP server for now.

mcp.title: GitHub - ahrefs/ahrefs-mcp-server: Official Ahrefs MCP Server
OpenClaw | Ahrefs for Developers
mcp.snippet:
Follow these steps to add the Ahrefs MCP server to OpenClaw using `mcporter`.
- **Install mcporter**`npm install -g mcporter`. Alternatively, you can install it from the Gateway dashboard under Skills.
- **Add the Ahrefs MCP server**`mcporter config add ahrefs https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp`.
- **Generate an MCP token in Ahrefs.**
- Open the API keys report in your Ahrefs account: [https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys](https://app.ahrefs.com/account/api-keys)
- Generate a new MCP key.
- Copy the token.
- **Add your MCP token to the mcporter config.** Run: `mcporter config list`. Locate the path to the `mcporter` config JSON file and open it. Add your MCP token as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ahrefs": { "baseUrl": "https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_AHREFS_MCP_TOKEN_HERE" } } }, "imports": [] }
```
- **Test the connection.** Example: `mcporter call ahrefs.keywords-explorer-volume-history country=us keyword=seo`. If the setup is correct, the request should return data.

mcp.title: 15 Ahrefs MCP Use Cases for SEOs & Digital Marketers
mcp.snippet:
With the recent launch of our remote MCP server, anyone can now chat directly with Ahrefs data to get actionable SEO insights.
MCP, which stands for Model Context Protocol, is an open standard that companies can use to integrate their external tools and data with compatible AI assistants.

Our new MCP server, which integrates with popular AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, offers the ability to automate these and countless other processes to gain insights at scale.

Available on Ahrefs Lite, Standard, Advanced and Enterprise plans, you’ll now be able to tap directly into our API without needing to know how to code.

Our [MCP help docs](https://docs.ahrefs.com/docs/mcp/reference/introduction) provide the full details on how to link your Ahrefs account to your preferred AI assistant.
There are guides to five popular AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot Studio. Alternatively, you can use our remote connection URL directly: `https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp`.
While you can get the same great functionality from the ChatGPT integration as Claude, MCP connectors are in beta in ChatGPT, and that’s noticeable at times.

Tools don’t always know to use the Ahrefs MCP server versus searching the web, so it’s highly recommended that you’re specific about that, starting requests with “Use the Ahrefs MCP server” or “Using the Ahrefs MCP server,...”.
Assume that I may have had to add that to the following prompts if they didn’t route through the Ahrefs MCP connection automatically.
